# SOP-P2-L3-01 Line startup - Machining line
Revision: Rev B
Plant: P2, line P2-L3
Equipment: EQ-P2-L3-RR01, EQ-P2-L3-HT02, EQ-P2-L3-IH03
Related documents: MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3, SB-1003, SB-1023

Purpose
1. Provide standardized startup steps for P2-L3 machining line to ensure safe, repeatable operation of roll rectifier, heat treat furnace, and induction billet heater. Background and rationale are included to support operator decisions and record keeping.

Scope
2. Applies to operators, line leads, and maintenance personnel responsible for EQ-P2-L3-RR01, EQ-P2-L3-HT02, and EQ-P2-L3-IH03 during first-shift startup and changeover into production.

Preconditions
3. Ensure all maintenance work orders are closed and tags removed for the equipment listed. Verify that lockout/tagout status is cleared by maintenance and that any temporary guards removed are refitted and secured. Confirm that required spare parts and consumables are on the line staging area.

Safety and PPE
4. Required PPE: safety glasses with side shields, hearing protection, cut-resistant gloves, flame-resistant coveralls, and safety shoes. Follow plant respiratory program where applicable. No PPE sizes, classes, or other numeric ratings are specified in this procedure; use PPE per site policy.

Key safety considerations and controls
5. Verify emergency stops function on EQ-P2-L3-RR01, EQ-P2-L3-HT02, and EQ-P2-L3-IH03 before energizing. Confirm ventilation and exhaust systems for the furnace are online. Observe clear access to aisles and emergency exits. If any interlock fails, stop and notify maintenance.

Required readings and references
6. Review MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3 for maintenance history of EQ-P2-L3-IH03. Review SB-1003 and SB-1023 for safety bulletins applicable to this line prior to startup.

Operational prerequisites
7. Check raw material staging and confirm billets are within acceptable supplier specification as documented in the production order. Confirm coolant and lubricant stocks are available for immediate replenishment.

Critical machine-specific settings and consumables
8. The coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03) is 72 L/min. Confirm flow meets this minimum before energizing the induction coils. Record flow reading in the startup log.

9. The lubricant part number for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is CFW-LUB-373. Confirm lubricant is installed to the system and that the reservoir level meets the fill requirement per manufacturer guidance.

Startup procedure (numbered steps)
10. Pre-start inspection
  10.1 Walk the line and visually inspect guards, couplings, instrument connections, and conveyors feeding EQ-P2-L3-RR01, EQ-P2-L3-HT02, and EQ-P2-L3-IH03.
  10.2 Verify that fire suppression zones and detector indicators are in normal state. If any detector shows alarm, do not proceed.
  10.3 Confirm that the lubrication and coolant reservoirs are at the required levels and that filters are installed.

11. Electrical and control verification
  11.1 Position control in local mode for each piece of equipment and ensure HMI displays communication with PLC.
  11.2 Enable power to control panels and observe for fault codes. If a fault appears, reference SB-1003, stop, and escalate.

12. Fluid systems commissioning
  12.1 Start coolant pumps and observe supply line for leaks and steady flow. Specifically confirm EQ-P2-L3-IH03 coil cooling water meets the specified minimum flow: 72 L/min.
  12.2 Pressurize lubrication lines and cycle the pump to purge air. Verify lubricant part number CFW-LUB-373 is in use for EQ-P2-L3-HT02.

13. Mechanical runout and slow-speed verification
  13.1 Jog conveyors and feed mechanisms at low speed using local controls. Listen for unusual noises and monitor vibration indicators. Stop immediately if abnormal sounds or interlocks trigger.
  13.2 Confirm roll rectifier positioning and alignment with sample billet hand-feed; ensure no pinch points are exposed.

14. Warm-up and functional checks
  14.1 Initiate furnace warm-up per control HMI sequence and monitor for stable indications before permitting billet introduction. Maintain clear signage during warm-up.
  14.2 Bring induction heater to permitted operating mode only when coil cooling flow and interlocks are confirmed.

15. Test piece and verification
  15.1 Run a single test billet through the sequence at approved feed rate. Inspect final part for gross dimensional conformance and surface quality as a first-article check.
  15.2 If defects are found, halt production and document findings. Refer to MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3 for troubleshooting EQ-P2-L3-IH03-related heating anomalies.

Records to keep
16. Maintain the startup logbook with entries for:
  - Date and time of startup.
  - Operator and line lead names.
  - Confirmation entries for coil cooling flow reading, explicitly recording the reading used to verify the 72 L/min minimum for EQ-P2-L3-IH03.
  - Confirmation of lubricant CFW-LUB-373 usage for EQ-P2-L3-HT02.
  - Any faults or maintenance actions taken and reference to work order numbers.
  - First-article inspection results and disposition.

Examples and rationale
17. Example: If coil cooling flow reads below the required minimum, do not energize the induction coils. Low coil cooling increases risk of coil damage and unsafe heating conditions; this is why a defined minimum is recorded and enforced. Consult MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3 for component inspection guidance.

18. Example: If lubricant reservoir for EQ-P2-L3-HT02 is topped with an alternate product, tag out the furnace and notify maintenance; record the event and the corrective action. Proper lubricant CFW-LUB-373 is required to maintain bearing life and heat transfer performance.

Nonconformance and stop criteria
19. Any departure from required interlocks, confirmed low coolant flow, unknown lubricant, or unresolved alarm conditions must result in immediate halt of startup and escalation to maintenance and the line manager.

Sign-off
20. Operators and supervisors must sign the startup log. Sign-off fields should include printed name, role, signature, and time. The line lead verifies that all checklist items were completed and that records are entered into the document control system.

Revision and document control
21. Changes to this procedure require approval per document control. See SB-1003 and SB-1023 for document and safety bulletin management processes.
